title: NIST Disaster & Failure Studies / NCST as structural-failure investigation and correction-memory rail
summary: NIST DFS/NCST is encoded as building/structural failure investigation infrastructure: it can deploy teams, conduct long technical investigations, preserve evidence, and issue recommendations or code/practice-change surfaces, but it is not a guarantee of fast final causation or correction infusion.

status_history.note: Added as structural failure lane visibility/correction rail.

subjects.name: NIST Disaster and Failure Studies / NCST

claims.claim: NIST Disaster and Failure Studies describes research into building, infrastructure, and emergency-response performance and notes that such failures can arise from design, construction, material, or other errors.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: NIST’s NCST Act page says the 2002 Act authorizes NIST teams, modeled after the NTSB, and notes that investigations may take years; Champlain Towers South is represented as a current NCST investigation surface.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The rail is encoded as correction memory rather than correction proof: NIST can investigate, recommend, and support code/practice change, but the cube must separately track whether recommendations are adopted and infused.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

evidence_refs.support_type: correction memory versus correction infusion pattern

limitations: Existence of the rail does not prove signal capture, adoption, enforcement, or correction infusion.

type_payload.infrastructure_class: structural/building failure investigation and recommendation rail
type_payload.signal_capture_model: post-event deployment, evidence preservation, technical investigation, public updates, reports, and recommendations

handling_notes: Represent infrastructure as a visibility/correction rail, not a guarantee of safety.
Avoid implying that absence of records means absence of risk.
